title: The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show
paragraphs: NBC comedy/situation-comedy and music vehicle starring fictionalized versions of Phil Harris and Alice Faye with a recurring family, band and supporting cast.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Fitch Bandwagon: Phil Harris-Alice Faye era (September 29, 1946 to May 23, 1948) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show: Rexall era (October 3, 1948 to June 4, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show: RCA era (October 1, 1950 to June 18, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Elliott Lewis (performer), Phil Harris (performer), Alice Faye (performer), Bill Forman (announcer), Walter Tetley (performer), Anne Whitfield (performer), and Jeanine Roos (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].
The stories often return to music, bands and performance, family and domestic life, money, shopping and household finances, radio work and broadcasting, pets and animals, and travel and vacation.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar domestic and family situation comedy, Commercial sponsorship in network radio comedy, and Hollywood celebrity adapted to radio domestic comedy.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], and [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]].
